name: Astra centre kit cell 2 (r0 c2)
label: monster_overworld/astra-centre-kit-2 (칸 2226)
reasons: 화풍: 칸 정보량이 기준보다 훨씬 낮음 (2/4)

surfaces.part: window or dormer opening with cream and blue panes at left

answer.evidence: This is a 16x16 kit cell filled edge to edge by a sloped roof plane (evidence c). In columns x=8 and x=11 the shingle courses repeat as a light edge line at rows 1, 9 and 13, with darker rows below each: row 4 is darkest (#0a3f46), rows 6-8 are dark and row 12 is dark. At left, rows 7-13 hold a cream and blue window set in a dark navy frame. That is a vertical face of about 7 rows under the roof. The cell is a fragment, so the roof dominates and the front face is small. No isometric side face is drawn. The dark column at x~4 is only the frame outline.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single tile-sized teal block, about 16-17 px square, with a small pale detail. It has no readable roof, walls, door or windows, so it does not read as a whole building like the references, which are 100+ px wide with scalloped tile roofs, timber and plaster, and shaded stone. The measured facts do not argue against it: 12 visible tones per tile matches h101's 12, near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edges are tinted rather than neutral, so the outline is a dark teal tone and not near-black. The failure is structural. Only about 3 lightness steps are readable on its main material against 5-6 on the references. It has no per-tile roof highlights, no stone-by-stone shading and no plaster speckle, so the building lacks the references' visible information at that scale. It cannot sit next to the references as a building, so it fails.

surfaces.part: lower tile course / wall band with inset cream window or door at left

answer.evidence: This is a full-width 16x16 kit cell filled with teal tile courses. In columns x=8 and x=11 a light edge line at row 1 is followed by mid and dark rows, with the darkest row at row 4. Rows 6-8 form a dark band, and a light edge line at row 9 is followed by shadow at row 12. Another light line at row 13 and mid rows 14-15 form a lower band. These stepped courses (light line, then darker shadow) read as a sloped tile roof plane, so I count rows 0-8 as the top surface. A dark-framed cream panel at the left (rows 7-13 in x=4) reads as a vertical window or door face. The cell is a fragment, so the front face is only partly shown and this reading is moderately uncertain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single 16x16 teal tile, with a light dot and a pale band on a teal block. It has no roof, walls, door or windows, so it is not a whole building and does not match the building references. The measured facts are fine for one tile: 12 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 in the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted. Those numbers do not make up for the missing structure. The references carry about 5-6 shading steps per material across roof tiles, timber and stone, with per-tile highlights. The candidate shows only about 4 teal steps and no multi-material building structure. Because it is a fragment or cell, not a building, it cannot be accepted next to the references. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: teal tiled roof plane (fills the right and centre of the cell)
small cream and blue window or panel at left, inside a dark frame

answer.evidence: The cell is a 16x16 fill tile. Columns x=8 and x=11 show roof tile courses over all 16 rows: light course lines at rows 1, 9 and 13, with dark shadow lines at rows 4 and 12. This is a sloped roof plane (c). No wall or front face runs the full width below it. The only vertical element is a small cream and blue panel at the left (x about 1-4, rows 7-11) inside a dark frame, and the roof continues to row 15 beside it. That gives fewer than 3 front-face rows for the main body, so it reads as a roof-only, top-down slab piece. The classification is moderately uncertain because this is one cell of a larger kit.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single tile-sized teal object, about 16x20 source pixels. It has no roof, no wall/door/window structure and no building silhouette, so it is not a whole building like the two references. The measured facts are fine: 12 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges are tinted. Those figures come from a very small, densely packed area and do not make up for the missing structure. By eye the object has only about 3 readable lightness steps, with a pale highlight dot and a dark teal edge, while the references have about 6 steps on their roofs plus per-tile highlights, plaster speckle and individually shaded stones. It has no large-scale material ramps, so it falls well short of the reference as a building. This is probably a wrong crop or a misplaced cell, since the cell does not hold a complete building.

surfaces.part: left dark-framed cream/blue opening (window or door)

answer.evidence: The 16x16 cell is fully opaque. Rows 0-15 are repeating teal tile courses (light row, mid, dark; for example rows 1-5, 5-9, 9-13) that read as a roof plane. The only other element is a dark-outlined cream opening at the left (rows 6-13, x about 3-9). It is a small cut-in, not a wall face. There is no wall or front face of 3 or more rows under the roof, and no eave line that hands over to a south face. This cell shows only roof or top surface, so it reads as a flat slab and not as a roof over a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny teal block of about one tile with a small pale spot. It has no roof, no wall/door/window structure and no building silhouette, so it does not match the building references, which are large multi-tile houses with scalloped tile roofs, timber or stone walls and doors. Its 12 distinct colours in total equal the references' per-tile tone count, but the references carry that richness across a whole house, while here it is squeezed into a single small cell. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted. I count about 3 readable lightness steps on the main teal material against 5-6 on the references' roofs and walls. Nothing like the references' per-tile roof scallops, plaster speckle or stone-by-stone shading is visible. As a whole-building piece it reads as a sparse fragment, much thinner than the references.
